title: Riftwatch handoff — summary and playbook notes
content:
Purpose: quick inbound for next on-call; consolidated observations across the 02:00–10:00 UTC watch, notable incidents, temporary mitigations, and proposed playbook edits.

Quick summary:
- No Sev1s during shift. One Sev2 (cache-thrashing causing elevated token latency for hosted-api route /v1/generate) that surfaced 03:14–04:22 UTC and was mitigated with routing changes + autoscaler bump.
- Two customer-impacting error spikes tied to a canary model rollout; upstream rollback completed at 04:55 UTC.
- Several flaky alerts from the region health monitor (eu-west-1) — noisy but non-actionable; suggested tuning in alert thresholds.

What I observed (timeline):
- 03:10 UTC: sudden 3x P95 token-latency on api-hosted-1 /v1/generate; correlated with tiny but steady rise in prefix cache misses and a jump in KV eviction rates on ded-pool-3.
- 03:14 UTC: alerts triggered: LAT-P95 > 900ms, KV-EVICT > threshold.
- 03:20 UTC: triage showed heavy small-sequence traffic from two enterprise customers (CUST-A, CUST-C) — likely retried bursts.
- 03:30 UTC: routed 30% of traffic off ded-pool-3 to fallback-pool (compatible model-variant v2-q4) using smart-routing policy; immediate P95 improvement to ~420ms.
- 03:45 UTC: autoscaling policy executed: added 2 instances to ded-pool-3 (g5-16x). KV eviction stabilized by 04:05 UTC.
- 04:10 UTC: noticed higher 5xx rates on canary model service (model-onboard/canary-2027-11-20). Decision to rollback to model v1.9 at 04:30 UTC. 5xx resolved by 04:55 UTC.

Temporary mitigations performed (do not assume persistent fixes):
- Traffic routing: applied short-lived route weight change to shift 30% traffic off ded-pool-3 to fallback-pool for 45 minutes.
- Autoscaler bump: manual override to ensure two extra instances remained active for 1 hour after spike.
- Rate-limits: activated soft rate-limiting for the two noisy customers for 20 minutes while we stabilized.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- Primary: workload pattern changed (many small sequences with repeated prefix) causing prefix-KV churn on ded-pool-3; eviction thrash reduced effective cache hit-rate and increased token compute.
- Secondary: canary model introduced slightly higher memory pressure and more aggressive KV allocations which amplified eviction under bursty load.

Immediate next actions (owners & ETA):
- Ethan M: expand observability on KV cache metrics (emit per-pool eviction histograms) — ETA 2027-11-22.
- Lena Z: draft alert tuning proposal for eu-west-1 health monitor (raise P95 trigger, require sustained window 6m) — ETA 2027-11-23.
- Marcus O'N: follow up with models team about canary memory footprint difference and revert checklist — ETA 2027-11-21.
- Sofia P (me): reconcile on-call notes into ops-playbooks PR with runbook edits (see linked PR) — ETA 2027-11-21.

Runbook deltas / playbook notes (suggested edits):
1) Prefix cache thrash playbook: add a decision node to route >=25% of traffic off a pool when KV-EVICT spikes > 3x baseline AND P95 increases > 50% within 10m. Include the exact routing command used: "infra route update --pool ded-pool-3 --weight -30 --to fallback-pool --reason 'kv-evict-thrash-2027-11-20'".
2) Canary rollback checklist: explicitly check model memory allocation delta and KV allocation patterns before promoting canary; add step to notify SRE-runbook channel with the canary commit and observed OOM/KV metrics.
3) Eu-west-1 alert tuning: replace single-point P95 alert with a composite: (P95 > 800ms for 6m AND error-rate > 0.5%) OR (KV-EVICT > 3x baseline for 5m).

Open follow-ups and backlog items:
- Create an automated canary-safety gate for KV allocation (ticket: JIRA-OPS-1342). Owner: Marcus O'N.
- Long-term: consider adding per-customer burst protection to reduce retry cascades (spike limiter at routing layer). Owner: product/hosting.
- Audit autoscaler policies for ded-pool-3 to ensure quicker scale-out on KV pressure signals in addition to CPU/GPU utilization. Owner: infra-scaling team.

Commands & quick checks (for incoming oncall):
- Check P95 and KV eviction: "observability query --metric p95_token_ms --filter pool=ded-pool-3" and "observability query --metric kv_evictions --filter pool=ded-pool-3"
- Re-route traffic (rollback mitigation): "infra route update --pool ded-pool-3 --weight -30 --to fallback-pool --expires 00:45 --reason 'handoff mitigation'"
- Temp scale: "infra autoscale override --pool ded-pool-3 --instances +2 --expires 01:00 --reason 'oncall manual bump'"

Contacts & escalation path:
- Primary oncall (infra): Ethan Morales (pager)
- Secondary SRE: Lena Zhang (slack DM)
- Models lead: Marcus O'Neil (pager)
- Escalate to engineering director if Sev2 persists for >2h or any customer sees >30% error-rate sustained >30m.

Notes to incoming:
- Expect some noisy eu-west-1 alerts — we've annotated them and plan to tune thresholds. If you see identical alert signatures to this shift, focus on KV-EVICT correlations before taking disruptive actions.
- Avoid immediate large-scale routing changes; prefer staged percentage shifts and watch 5m windows.
- If you need to escalate model rollback, follow the new quick-rollback steps added to the playbook (linked in PR).

Appendix (observed metrics snapshot at peak 03:20 UTC):
- P95 token latency (ded-pool-3): 980ms (baseline 300ms)
- KV eviction rate: 4.6k/min (baseline 600/min)
- 5xx rate (canary model): 2.1% -> increased to 8.9% during rollout
- Routed traffic fraction to fallback-pool: 30% from 03:30–04:15 UTC

End of notes. Please ping me or leave updates in the SRE handoff thread (slack) if you take any of the open followups so I can update playbook PR. — Sofia
